1.title: Troubleshooting Applications and Container Logs
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Troubleshooting Applications and Container Logs. It covers the exam area Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The method: top-down, one command at a time. Pod status words and what they mean. Reading logs: every variant. Break-and-fix catalog. Useful debugging tools. Practice with nine hands-on labs worth fifty-one points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Troubleshooting (thirty percent, the largest domain). Practice in this module: nine labs, fifty-one points, about fifty-one minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: The method: top-down, one command at a time
1.text: The method: top-down, one command at a time. The figure shows this: The troubleshooting method.

1.title: The method: top-down, one command at a time, continued
1.text: The method: top-down, one command at a time. Never guess. Follow the evidence from the outside in. What is the state? kube control get pods dash o wide (S T A T U S, R E A D Y, R E S T A R T S, N O D E). What does Kubernetes say? kube control describe pod p: read the Events at the bottom, then State, Last State, Reason, Exit Code. What did the app say? kube control logs p (and the previous flag ). Is it the object or the node? Check the Deployment ( kube control get deploy, kube control rollout status ), then the node (Module twelve). Fix, then verify with the same command that showed the problem. kube control get events the sort by flag set to dot last Timestamp dash n ns lists recent events in time order across the namespace. Use dash A for all namespaces.

1.title: Pod status words and what they mean
1.text: Pod status words and what they mean. Pending. Meaning: not scheduled, or waiting for a volume. First command: describe pod (Failed Scheduling). Usual fix: resources, selector, taint, P V C (Modules six, ten). Container Creating. Meaning: scheduled, but the container cannot be set up. First command: describe pod events. Usual fix: missing Config Map or Secret or P V C; C N I (Container Network Interface) or image problem. Err Image Pull or Image Pull Back Off. Meaning: cannot pull the image. First command: describe pod ("Failed to pull image"). Usual fix: wrong image name or tag, private registry needs an image pull Secret. Crash Loop Back Off. Meaning: container starts and exits repeatedly. First command: logs the previous flag, describe (exit code). Usual fix: bad command, missing env or config, failing dependency, wrong probe. Exam tip: For Image Pull Back Off, read describe pod and check the image name and tag.

1.title: Pod status words and what they mean, continued
1.text: Pod status words and what they mean. Create Container Error, Run Container Error. Meaning: runtime cannot start the process. First command: describe pod. Usual fix: wrong command (executable not found), bad mount. Init zero slash one, Init Error. Meaning: an init container has not finished. First command: logs p dash c init. Usual fix: the thing it waits for does not exist yet. Error, O O M Killed. Meaning: container died. First command: describe (Last State: Reason, Exit Code). Usual fix: O O M Killed equals memory limit too low (exit one hundred thirty-seven). Running but zero slash one ready. Meaning: readiness probe failing. First command: describe (Readiness probe failed). Usual fix: wrong probe port or path or app not up.

1.title: Pod status words and what they mean, continued
1.text: Pod status words and what they mean. Terminating for a long time. Meaning: finalizer or node down. First command: describe, node state. Usual fix: force delete only as a last step. Exit codes: zero normal, one application error, one hundred thirty-seven killed (O O M or S I G K I L L), one hundred forty-three terminated by S I G T E R M.

1.title: Reading logs: every variant
1.text: Reading logs: every variant. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: For a container that keeps crashing, read the last run with kube control logs the previous flag.

1.title: Reading logs: every variant, continued
1.text: Reading logs: every variant. Multi-container Pods: kube control logs pod with no dash c prints only one container (the first one, or the one named in the kube control dot Kubernetes dot io slash default container annotation) and a "Defaulted container" notice. Always name the container with dash c when the task names one (Lab eleven point one). kube control get pod p dash o json path dot spec dot containers dot name lists them; init containers are in dot spec dot init containers. the tail flag with a selector defaults to ten lines per Pod; use the tail flag set to -one for all lines (Lab eleven point nine).

1.title: Reading logs: every variant, continued
1.text: Reading logs: every variant. A crash loop's real message is in the previous flag. The current container may have no output yet (Lab eleven point two). In the lab cluster the previous flag sometimes answers "unable to retrieve container logs" (the old container was already cleaned up); then plain kube control logs pod shows the same message, because the app prints it on every attempt. Logs are the container's stdout and stderr. A path inside the container is read with kube control exec p -- cat slash path.

1.title: Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs)
1.text: Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs). Image Pull Back Off (Lab eleven point three). Cause found by: describe pod: "manifest unknown" or "not found". Fix: kube control set image deploy slash web engine X engine X alpine. Crash Loop Back Off, log says "D B H O S T is required" (Lab eleven point four). Cause found by: kube control logs. Fix: kube control set env deploy slash worker D B H O S T db dot internal. Container Creating, event "configmap... not found" (Lab eleven point five). Cause found by: describe pod (Failed Mount). Fix: create the Config Map; the kubelet retries and the Pod starts by itself, no delete needed. O O M Killed, restarts (Lab eleven point six). Cause found by: describe: Last State Reason O O M Killed, exit one hundred thirty-seven. Fix: raise resources dot limits dot memory; recreate the Pod (Pod resources are immutable). Init zero slash one (Lab eleven point seven). Cause found by: logs pod dash c init: "waiting for db". Fix: create the missing Service or dependency.

1.title: Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs), continued
1.text: Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs). Create Container Error (Lab eleven point eight). Cause found by: event: "executable file not found in $P A T H". Fix: fix the command (typo sleeep ). Pod with wrong probe (Lab five point nine). Cause found by: describe: Liveness probe failed. Fix: correct the probe. Pending (Labs six point eight, ten point six, ten point seven). Cause found by: Failed Scheduling events. Fix: resources, class name, access mode. Editing rules: a Pod's image can be changed in place with kube control set image (and kube control edit ), but most other Pod fields cannot: delete and recreate (use the force flag the grace period flag zero to avoid waiting). For Deployments, edit the template and the rollout replaces the Pods. Exam tip: Exit code one hundred thirty-seven means the container was killed for using too much memory; exit code one means the application failed.

1.title: Useful debugging tools
1.text: Useful debugging tools. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Work top down: get, describe, logs, then fix and verify.

1.title: Lab 11.1: container logs
1.text: Lab eleven point one: container logs. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace lg one, the Pod multi has two containers, app and side. Save the log output of the container side (only that container) to about slash answers slash side dot log on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 11.1: container logs, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n lg one logs multi. Then kube control dash n lg one logs multi dash c side about slash answers slash side dot log. Then cat about slash answers slash side dot log. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 11.2: previous logs
1.text: Lab eleven point two: previous logs. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace lg two, the Pod crashy keeps restarting. Find the error message the application prints just before it exits and save that one line, exactly as printed, to about slash answers slash error dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 11.2: previous logs, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n lg two get pod crashy. Then for i in seq one twenty do. Then out kube control dash n lg two logs crashy the previous flag two slash dev slash null then pipe to then pipe to kube control dash n lg two logs crashy two slash dev, and so on. Then case out in then pipe to unable to retrieve then pipe to not found sleep four break esac. Then done. Then echo out about slash answers slash error dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash error dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 11.3: fix image pull
1.text: Lab eleven point three: fix image pull. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app three, the Deployment web (two replicas) shows Image Pull Back Off. Find the cause and fix the Deployment so that both replicas run engine X alpine. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.3: fix image pull, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app three describe pod dash l app web then pipe to grep dash i -A three Failed to pull then pipe to head -six. Then kube control dash n app three set image deployment web engine X engine X alpine. Then kube control dash n app three rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.4: fix missing env
2.text: Lab eleven point four: fix missing env. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app four, the Pods of the Deployment worker crash with a clear message in their logs. Read the log, then fix the Deployment (do not change the image or the command) so that the Pods run stably with the required setting D B H O S T db dot internal. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.4: fix missing env, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app four logs deploy slash worker the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n app four set env deployment worker D B H O S T db dot internal. Then kube control dash n app four rollout status deployment worker the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.5: fix missing configmap
2.text: Lab eleven point five: fix missing configmap. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app five, the Pod site is stuck in Container Creating. Find out why (read the events) and fix it without deleting the Pod: the Pod needs a Config Map site config whose key index dot html contains Hello from config, mounted at slash usr slash share slash engine X slash html. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.5: fix missing configmap, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app five describe pod site then pipe to grep dash i -A three Failed Mount. Then kube control dash n app five create configmap site config the from literal flag set to index dot html Hello from config. Then kube control dash n app five wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash site the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.6: oomkilled
2.text: Lab eleven point six: oomkilled. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app six, the Pod hungry restarts all the time. Find the reason in the Pod's status. The container needs about forty mebibytes B of memory to run. Recreate the Pod hungry (same image and command) with a memory limit of one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes so that it runs stably with zero restarts. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.6: oomkilled, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app six get pod hungry dash o json path dot status dot container Statuses zero dot last State dot terminated dot reason echo. Then kube control dash n app six delete pod hungry the force flag the grace period flag zero. kube control dash n app six apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n app six wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash hungry the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then sleep fifteen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.7: fix init container
2.text: Lab eleven point seven: fix init container. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app seven, the Pod api is stuck in Init zero slash one: its init container waits until the D N S name db resolves inside the namespace. Without changing the Pod, make the Pod start. The name db must be the name of a Service in app seven that selects the existing Pod database (label app database, engine X on port eighty). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.7: fix init container, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app seven get pod api. Then kube control dash n app seven logs api dash c wait db the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n app seven expose pod database the name flag set to db the port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n app seven wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash api the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.8: fix wrong command
2.text: Lab eleven point eight: fix wrong command. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app eight, the Deployment ticker cannot start its container (the status shows an error such as Create Container Error or Run Container Error ). Find the cause in the Pod events and fix the Deployment so that two replicas run. The container is supposed to run the command sleep three thousand six hundred. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.8: fix wrong command, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app eight describe pod dash l app ticker then pipe to grep dash i dash E executable file not found then pipe to Error then pipe to head -three. Then kube control dash n app eight patch deployment ticker the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash command, value sleep, and so on. Then kube control dash n app eight rollout status deployment ticker the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 11.9: logs by label
2.text: Lab eleven point nine: logs by label. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace lg nine, the Deployment svc has three Pods (label app svc ). Each Pod printed one line starting with error at startup, among other lines. Collect the error lines of all three Pods into about slash answers slash errors dot txt on the host (one line per Pod, no other lines). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 11.9: logs by label, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n lg nine logs dash l app svc the tail flag set to -one grep ^error about slash answers slash errors dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash errors dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Where do you find the error of a container that is in Crash Loop Back Off? Answer: In kube control logs pod the previous flag and the exit code in kube control describe pod. Question two. What does exit code one hundred thirty-seven and O O M Killed indicate? Answer: The container was killed for exceeding its memory limit. Question three. A Pod has two containers. How do you read the second one's logs? Answer: kube control logs pod dash c container name.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. How do you read the logs of all Pods with a label, all lines? Answer: kube control logs dash l key value the tail flag set to -one. Question five. A Pod is stuck in Container Creating and the event says the Config Map is not found. What do you do? Answer: Create the Config Map; the kubelet retries and the Pod starts. Question six. Which command lists namespace events in time order? Answer: kube control get events the sort by flag set to dot last Timestamp.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What does Init zero slash one mean and where do you look? Answer: The first of one init container has not finished; read kube control logs pod dash c init container. Question eight. Can you edit the resource limits of a running Pod? Answer: No; delete and recreate it (or change the Deployment template).

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Method: get, describe (Events), logs, then fix and verify. Image problems: Image Pull Back Off - greater than tag or name; describe pod. Crashes: logs the previous flag; exit one hundred thirty-seven equals O O M; one equals app error. Stuck creating: missing Config Map, Secret, P V C; read events. Logs: dash c container, the previous flag, dash l selector with the tail flag set to -one, dash f, the since flag. Init containers: logs dash c init; waits for a dependency. Immutable: Pod resources or commands: recreate; Deployments: edit the template. In the next module, we continue the course.
